title: Pair with a Given Sum

concept.title: Two pointers closing in
body: In a sorted array, put one pointer `l` at the smallest element and one pointer `r` at the largest. Look at their sum: if it is **too small**, only a bigger left element can help, so move `l` right. If it is **too big**, move `r` left. If it is right, you found the pair.

body.code:
l, r = 0, n - 1
while l < r:
    s = a[l] + a[r]
    if s == target: break
    if s < target: l += 1
    else: r -= 1

body: Every step discards one element that cannot be part of any answer, so the pointers meet after at most `n` steps. This beats trying all pairs, which needs about `n * n / 2` checks.

statement: You are given an array of `n` different integers sorted in increasing order and a number `target`. Exactly one pair of positions `i < j` has `a[i] + a[j] = target`. Print the two positions, counting from 1.
inputFormat: The second line has the `n` sorted integers.
outputFormat: Print `i` and `j` separated by a space, with `i < j`.
hints: Start with a pointer at each end.
If the sum is too small move the left pointer right, if too big move the right pointer left.
Print `l + 1` and `r + 1` because positions start at 1.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, target = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

explanation: Two pointers move towards each other. A sum that is too small can only grow by moving the left pointer, a sum that is too big can only shrink by moving the right pointer.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, target = map(int, input().split())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

l, rr = 0, n - 1
while l < rr:
    s = a[l] + a[rr]
    if s == target:
        break
    if s < target:
        l += 1
    else:
        rr -= 1
print(l + 1, rr + 1)
